subject: Containment verification & technical walkthrough — August 22 service disruption
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: ops@fintecha.com
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 16:10:00 -0400
Subject: Containment verification & technical walkthrough — August 22 service disruption

Hi Sam / Fintecha ops team,

Thank you again for the patience while we investigated the instability you observed this morning (roughly 09:05–09:40 PT). We’re sending a short technical readout with the containment actions we applied and next steps to provide a reproducible verification package.

What happened (short):
- At ~09:05 PT your production inference fleet experienced an increase in 503/timeout errors and mid-stream token drops for a subset of long-running sessions.
- We immediately routed traffic away from the affected Dedicated pool and applied an emergency policy to pin sessions to stable kernels while we investigated.

Immediate containment (what we did):
- Isolated and drained the affected worker nodes (no user traffic routed to degraded instances).
- Rolled back a recent autoscaler binary that altered preemption behavior on pooled nodes.
- Re-enabled strict KV prefix caching for long-lived sessions to avoid partial KV eviction during high load.

Attachments: containment_logs_20260822.zip (logs, truncated traces), timeline-annotated-aug22.pdf (annotated event timeline).

Next steps:
1) Technical walkthrough tomorrow (08/23) 10:00 PT — we’ll present findings and run a shared verification against a controlled traffic sample.
2) Deliver a short remediation playbook (mitigation-playbook.md) with step-by-step verification steps and a small script to reproduce the degraded path.
3) We’ll keep a 24x7 on-call presence for the Fintecha environment through Friday to validate stability metrics.

We’ll follow up shortly with a more detailed timeline and the preliminary root cause hypotheses.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Containment verification & technical walkthrough — August 22 service disruption

Sam —

Below is the annotated timeline and our preliminary technical findings. We’ll walk through this in the 10:00 PT call and hand over the verification artifacts.

Annotated timeline (UTC):
- 2026-08-22T13:05:12Z — First elevated 5xx/timeout alerts triggered from your synthetic probes (5–7% error spike vs baseline).
- 2026-08-22T13:06:05Z — Autoscaler event: three worker nodes preempted and replaced within the Dedicated pool serving your workload.
- 2026-08-22T13:06:45Z — Partial KV cache writeback observed concurrent with kernel handoff on two replaced nodes; small proportion of sessions encountered missing KV shards.
- 2026-08-22T13:07:30Z — Token-generation stalls / partial responses observed for sessions with sequence length > 512.
- 2026-08-22T13:09:10Z — We enabled containment: drained affected nodes and applied kernel pinning to stable CPU/GPU drivers.
- 2026-08-22T13:15:42Z — Error rate returned to baseline; monitoring showed steady token throughput.

Preliminary root cause (hypothesis):
- Trigger: concurrent autoscaler replacements combined with a regression in a recent autoscaler binary that altered graceful drain timing. The shorter drain window exposed a race where KV cache shards for large sessions were not consistently flushed to a shared backend before node termination.
- Effect: on a small subset of sessions (long sequences + quantized model variants), the missing KV shards led to an inconsistent state during token generation: generator resumed but with reduced context leading to stalls or early termination of streaming responses.
- Why quantized variants were hit: quantized kernels share a different caching path and, in a narrow window, performed a deferred writeback that did not complete before node tear-down.

Planned corrective actions (owners & ETA):
- Rollback the autoscaler binary to the prior stable build: owner David Kim — ETA 2026-08-23 02:00Z.
- Add guard rails to the drain sequence to ensure KV shards are fully flushed or re-routed: owner Hannah Schmitt — ETA 2026-08-30.
- Add automated integration test covering graceful drain + KV flush semantics under heavy long-sequence traffic: owner Engineering (David) — ETA 2026-09-07.
- Deliver verification bundle (scripts + truncated logs + test harness): owner Neha Kapoor — ETA 2026-08-24 (attached link).

Evidence attached / available: containment_logs_20260822.zip (traces and node-level metrics), timeline-annotated-aug22.pdf. We will include a short reproduction script in the mitigation-playbook.md.

If any of these owners should be changed on your side for approvals, tell us and we’ll loop them in.

Neha

Sam / Maria —

Quick status update following our verification run this morning:
- The rollback of the autoscaler binary (David) completed at 02:05Z with no further preemption anomalies in the dedicated pool.
- We executed the reproduction harness on a mirrored environment and reproduced the partial-KV-miss behavior; the attached mitigation-playbook.md includes the command sequence we used.
- Owner commitments remain the same; Hannah will begin the drain-guard implementation this week and provide a PR reference by 2026-08-26.

Action items for Fintecha ops (short):
- Confirm receipt of the verification bundle and run the lightweight smoke test attached to the shared Drive link. We can stand up a joint session to watch logs live if helpful.
- Let us know if you want the rollback permanently applied to your Dedicated pool or prefer the conservative guard rails once implemented.

We’ll keep daily check-ins until you confirm there’s no recurrence. Thanks for the clear triage notes during the event — that made reproduction much faster.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
